02 / The scorecard

A December of highs and lows.

See the family verdict across all 25 days—and find out who was on an entirely different chocolate wavelength.

25 days. Seven critics. One very squiggly line.

The dark line is the family average. Add one or more people to compare their scores day by day; tap a day to see exactly who gave what.

A missing individual score is shown as a break, not a zero. Average scores use all available final ratings for that day. On mobile, swipe the graph sideways to see the full month.

The statistical tea leaves

A few more deliciously nerdy awards.

Explore all reviewer correlations

Pearson correlation of scores on shared chocolates (at least 10 shared days for the rankings below). A negative value indicates opposite rating patterns; correlation is different from simply giving the same numeric scores. The full table is sorted from most to least correlated.

A three- or five-day stretch is the unweighted mean of that period's daily averages, so each chocolate counts equally even if fewer people submitted scores. Some family members skipped days.

03 / Meet the tasting committee

Seven people.
Seven palates.

Everyone came to the same chocolates. Not everyone came to the same conclusions.

⚡
The Speedy Submitter

David

Reviewed 8 of 12 chocolates on the day they were opened — the highest same-day share (67%).

✷
The Completionist

Michael

The only person to score all 25 days. An act of admirable chocolate dedication.

♡
The Taste Twins

Erin + Michael

The most aligned frequent reviewers: r = 0.70 across 24 shared days.

Same-day means submitted before midnight on that chocolate’s calendar date. Correlations are Pearson correlations on days both reviewers scored; small samples can be noisy. Every reviewer saw a different subset of chocolates.

Photo sources, verification & attribution

All photographs come from Dandelion Chocolate’s official daily-unveil catalog. Each catalog entry directly connects its day, confection name, chocolatier and image. The linked reveal videos were published by Dandelion in November 2025; surviving product pages also identify the 2025 calendar.

The live site has some 2026 labels, so those labels alone were not used to date the photos. The day-specific catalog and its 2025 videos establish the associations shown here. The full provenance file in the editable project records URLs, file hashes, download dates and corrections to earlier guesses.

Image credit: Dandelion Chocolate’s official calendar photography; individual photographers are not named in the source. Copyright remains with the respective rights holders. These public assets have no identified open reuse license; attribution does not grant redistribution permission. This is an unofficial family review.
